INSERT INTO INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.AGENTS
WITH
first_names AS (
    SELECT ARRAY_CONSTRUCT(
        'James','Robert','Michael','David','William','Richard','Joseph','Thomas','Christopher','Daniel',
        'Matthew','Anthony','Mark','Steven','Paul','Andrew','Joshua','Kenneth','Kevin','Brian',
        'Sarah','Jennifer','Jessica','Emily','Amanda','Ashley','Megan','Stephanie','Nicole','Elizabeth',
        'Patricia','Linda','Barbara','Susan','Margaret','Dorothy','Lisa','Karen','Nancy','Betty',
        'Charles','Donald','George','Edward','Ronald','Timothy','Jason','Jeffrey','Ryan','Jacob',
        'Michelle','Kimberly','Donna','Carol','Ruth','Sharon','Laura','Cynthia','Kathleen','Amy',
        'Angela','Melissa','Deborah','Brenda','Rebecca','Diane','Shirley','Pamela','Sandra','Teresa'
    ) AS arr
),
last_names AS (
    SELECT ARRAY_CONSTRUCT(
        'Smith','Johnson','Williams','Brown','Jones','Garcia','Miller','Davis','Rodriguez','Martinez',
        'Hernandez','Lopez','Gonzalez','Wilson','Anderson','Thomas','Taylor','Moore','Jackson','Martin',
        'Lee','Perez','Thompson','White','Harris','Sanchez','Clark','Ramirez','Lewis','Robinson',
        'Walker','Young','Allen','King','Wright','Scott','Torres','Nguyen','Hill','Flores',
        'Green','Adams','Nelson','Baker','Hall','Rivera','Campbell','Mitchell','Carter','Roberts',
        'Turner','Phillips','Evans','Collins','Stewart','Morris','Murphy','Cook','Rogers','Morgan',
        'Peterson','Cooper','Reed','Bailey','Bell','Gomez','Kelly','Howard','Ward','Cox'
    ) AS arr
),
regions AS (
    SELECT ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('Northeast','Southeast','Midwest','West','Southwest') AS arr
),
region_states AS (
    SELECT ARRAY_CONSTRUCT(
        ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('NY','NJ','CT','MA','PA'),
        ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('FL','GA','NC','SC','VA'),
        ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('IL','OH','MI','IN','WI'),
        ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('CA','WA','OR','CO','NV'),
        ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('TX','AZ','NM','OK','LA')
    ) AS arr
),
specializations AS (
    SELECT ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('Auto','Home','Life','Health','Commercial') AS arr
),
raw_data AS (
    SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SEQ4()) AS rn
    FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 150))
)
SELECT
    'AGT-' || LPAD(rn::VARCHAR, 3, '0'),
    first_names.arr[UNIFORM(0, 69, RANDOM(rn))]::VARCHAR || ' ' || last_names.arr[UNIFORM(0, 69, RANDOM(rn + 1000))]::VARCHAR,
    regions.arr[MOD(rn - 1, 5)]::VARCHAR,
    region_states.arr[MOD(rn - 1, 5)][UNIFORM(0, 4, RANDOM(rn + 2000))]::VARCHAR,
    specializations.arr[MOD(FLOOR((rn - 1) / 5), 5)]::VARCHAR,
    'LIC-' || LPAD((100000 + rn * 7)::VARCHAR, 6, '0'),
    DATEADD('day', -UNIFORM(365, 3650, RANDOM(rn + 3000)), '2025-06-30'::DATE),
    CASE
        WHEN UNIFORM(1, 100, RANDOM(rn + 4000)) <= 15 THEN ROUND(UNIFORM(1.00, 2.50, RANDOM(rn + 4001))::DECIMAL(3,2), 2)
        WHEN UNIFORM(1, 100, RANDOM(rn + 4000)) <= 40 THEN ROUND(UNIFORM(2.51, 3.50, RANDOM(rn + 4002))::DECIMAL(3,2), 2)
        ELSE ROUND(UNIFORM(3.51, 5.00, RANDOM(rn + 4003))::DECIMAL(3,2), 2)
    END,
    UNIFORM(10, 120, RANDOM(rn + 5000)),
    CASE WHEN UNIFORM(1, 100, RANDOM(rn + 6000)) <= 90 THEN 'Active' ELSE 'Inactive' END
FROM raw_data, first_names, last_names, regions, region_states, specializations

INSERT INTO INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.BILLING
WITH
payment_methods AS (
    SELECT ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('Credit Card','Credit Card','Credit Card','ACH','ACH','ACH','Check','Wire') AS arr
),
policy_data AS (
    SELECT POLICY_ID, CUSTOMER_ID, PREMIUM_AMOUNT, START_DATE,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY POLICY_ID) AS pol_rn
    FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.POLICIES
),
raw_data AS (
    SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SEQ4()) AS rn FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 20000))
)
SELECT
    'INV-' || LPAD((80000 + r.rn)::VARCHAR, 6, '0'),
    p.POLICY_ID,
    p.CUSTOMER_ID,
    DATEADD('month', MOD(r.rn - 1, 30), p.START_DATE),
    DATEADD('day', 30, DATEADD('month', MOD(r.rn - 1, 30), p.START_DATE)),
    ROUND(p.PREMIUM_AMOUNT / 12, 2),
    CASE
        WHEN ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pay'), 100)) < 85 THEN ROUND(p.PREMIUM_AMOUNT / 12, 2)
        WHEN ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pay'), 100)) < 92 THEN ROUND(p.PREMIUM_AMOUNT / 12 * (0.3 + ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pp'), 50)) / 100.0), 2)
        ELSE 0.00
    END,
    CASE
        WHEN ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pay'), 100)) < 85 THEN 0.00
        WHEN ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pay'), 100)) < 92 THEN ROUND(p.PREMIUM_AMOUNT / 12 * (1.0 - (0.3 + ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pp'), 50)) / 100.0)), 2)
        ELSE ROUND(p.PREMIUM_AMOUNT / 12, 2)
    END,
    CASE
        WHEN ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pay'), 100)) >= 92 THEN ROUND((15 + ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'lf'), 60)))::DECIMAL(8,2), 2)
        WHEN ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pay'), 100)) >= 85 THEN ROUND((5 + ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'lf2'), 20)))::DECIMAL(8,2), 2)
        ELSE 0.00
    END,
    CASE
        WHEN ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pay'), 100)) < 85 THEN 'Paid'
        WHEN ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pay'), 100)) < 92 THEN 'Partial'
        ELSE 'Overdue'
    END,
    CASE
        WHEN ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pay'), 100)) < 92 THEN payment_methods.arr[ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pm'), 8))]::VARCHAR
        ELSE NULL
    END,
    CASE
        WHEN ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pay'), 100)) < 85 THEN DATEADD('day', ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pd'), 25)) - 5, DATEADD('month', MOD(r.rn - 1, 30), p.START_DATE))
        WHEN ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pay'), 100)) < 92 THEN DATEADD('day', 30 + ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pd2'), 30)), DATEADD('month', MOD(r.rn - 1, 30), p.START_DATE))
        ELSE NULL
    END
FROM raw_data r
CROSS JOIN payment_methods
JOIN policy_data p ON p.pol_rn = MOD(r.rn - 1, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.POLICIES)) + 1

INSERT INTO INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.AT_RISK_POLICIES
WITH
risk_categories AS (
    SELECT ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('Churn','Churn','Churn','Payment Default','Payment Default','Underinsured') AS arr
),
retention_actions AS (
    SELECT ARRAY_CONSTRUCT('Discount Offer','Agent Call','Auto-Renew Lock','Premium Reduction','Coverage Review','None') AS arr
),
risky_policies AS (
    SELECT
        p.POLICY_ID, p.CUSTOMER_ID, p.PREMIUM_AMOUNT, p.END_DATE,
        COALESCE(b.missed, 0) AS missed_payments,
        COALESCE(c.claim_count, 0) AS claims_filed,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(b.missed, 0) DESC, COALESCE(c.claim_count, 0) DESC, p.POLICY_ID) AS risk_rn
    FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.POLICIES p
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT POLICY_ID, COUNT(*) AS missed FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.BILLING WHERE PAYMENT_STATUS IN ('Overdue','Partial') GROUP BY POLICY_ID
    ) b ON b.POLICY_ID = p.POLICY_ID
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT POLICY_ID, COUNT(*) AS claim_count FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.CLAIMS GROUP BY POLICY_ID
    ) c ON c.POLICY_ID = p.POLICY_ID
    WHERE p.STATUS = 'Active'
    QUALIFY risk_rn <= 1200
)

    POLICY_ID,
    CUSTOMER_ID,

    ROUND(PREMIUM_AMOUNT * 12, 2),
    GREATEST(0, DATEDIFF('day', CURRENT_DATE(), END_DATE)),
    missed_payments,
    claims_filed,
    -20 + ABS(MOD(HASH(risk_rn, 'nps'), 100)),
    DATEADD('day', -(1 + ABS(MOD(HASH(risk_rn, 'lcd'), 89))), CURRENT_DATE()),

input.sql:
INSERT INTO INSURANCE_AI_HUB.DATA_QUALITY.DQ_RESULTS
WITH
rule_data AS (
    SELECT RULE_ID, TARGET_TABLE, THRESHOLD, SEVERITY,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY RULE_ID) AS rule_rn
    FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.DATA_QUALITY.DQ_RULES
),
raw_data AS (
    SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SEQ4()) AS rn FROM TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => 5000))
)
SELECT
    'DQR-RES-' || LPAD(r.rn::VARCHAR, 5, '0'),
    rd.RULE_ID,
    DATEADD('day', -MOD(r.rn - 1, 100), CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())::TIMESTAMP_NTZ,
    rd.TARGET_TABLE,
    CASE rd.TARGET_TABLE
        WHEN 'CUSTOMERS' THEN 5000 WHEN 'AGENTS' THEN 150 WHEN 'POLICIES' THEN 8000
        WHEN 'CLAIMS' THEN 3500 WHEN 'BILLING' THEN 20000 ELSE 1200
    END,
    -- PASSED_RECORDS
    CASE
        WHEN rd.RULE_ID IN ('DQR-001','DQR-002') THEN
            CASE rd.TARGET_TABLE WHEN 'CUSTOMERS' THEN 5000 - (50 + ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p1'), 250))) ELSE 5000 - ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p2'), 40)) END
        WHEN rd.RULE_ID IN ('DQR-034','DQR-040','DQR-042') THEN
            CASE rd.TARGET_TABLE WHEN 'CLAIMS' THEN 3500 - (20 + ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p3'), 130))) WHEN 'BILLING' THEN 20000 - (100 + ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p4'), 700))) ELSE 1200 - ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p5'), 25)) END
        ELSE
            CASE rd.TARGET_TABLE WHEN 'CUSTOMERS' THEN 5000 - ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p6'), 10)) WHEN 'AGENTS' THEN 150 WHEN 'POLICIES' THEN 8000 - ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p7'), 15)) WHEN 'CLAIMS' THEN 3500 - ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p8'), 8)) WHEN 'BILLING' THEN 20000 - ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p9'), 20)) ELSE 1200 - ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p10'), 5)) END
    END,
    -- FAILED_RECORDS
    CASE rd.TARGET_TABLE
        WHEN 'CUSTOMERS' THEN 5000 WHEN 'AGENTS' THEN 150 WHEN 'POLICIES' THEN 8000
        WHEN 'CLAIMS' THEN 3500 WHEN 'BILLING' THEN 20000 ELSE 1200
    END -
    CASE
        WHEN rd.RULE_ID IN ('DQR-001','DQR-002') THEN
            CASE rd.TARGET_TABLE WHEN 'CUSTOMERS' THEN 5000 - (50 + ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p1'), 250))) ELSE 5000 - ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p2'), 40)) END
        WHEN rd.RULE_ID IN ('DQR-034','DQR-040','DQR-042') THEN
            CASE rd.TARGET_TABLE WHEN 'CLAIMS' THEN 3500 - (20 + ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p3'), 130))) WHEN 'BILLING' THEN 20000 - (100 + ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p4'), 700))) ELSE 1200 - ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p5'), 25)) END
        ELSE
            CASE rd.TARGET_TABLE WHEN 'CUSTOMERS' THEN 5000 - ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p6'), 10)) WHEN 'AGENTS' THEN 150 WHEN 'POLICIES' THEN 8000 - ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p7'), 15)) WHEN 'CLAIMS' THEN 3500 - ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p8'), 8)) WHEN 'BILLING' THEN 20000 - ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p9'), 20)) ELSE 1200 - ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'p10'), 5)) END
    END,
    -- PASS_RATE
    ROUND(CASE
        WHEN rd.RULE_ID IN ('DQR-001','DQR-002') THEN 92.00 + ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pr1'), 500)) / 100.0
        WHEN rd.RULE_ID IN ('DQR-034','DQR-040','DQR-042') THEN 88.00 + ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pr2'), 800)) / 100.0
        ELSE 97.00 + ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'pr3'), 300)) / 100.0
    END::DECIMAL(5,2), 2),
    CASE
        WHEN rd.RULE_ID IN ('DQR-001','DQR-002') AND ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'st1'), 100)) < 40 THEN 'Fail'
        WHEN rd.RULE_ID IN ('DQR-034','DQR-040','DQR-042') AND ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'st2'), 100)) < 30 THEN 'Fail'
        WHEN ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'st3'), 100)) < 5 THEN 'Warning'
        ELSE 'Pass'
    END,
    CASE WHEN ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'es'), 100)) < 15 THEN '{"sample_ids":["CUST-00142","CUST-03891"],"issue":"null_value"}' ELSE NULL END,
    50 + ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'et'), 4950)),
    CASE WHEN ABS(MOD(HASH(r.rn, 'rb'), 10)) = 0 THEN 'Manual' ELSE 'Scheduled' END
FROM raw_data r
JOIN rule_data rd ON rd.rule_rn = MOD(r.rn - 1, 50) + 1

INSERT INTO INSURANCE_AI_HUB.DATA_QUALITY.DQ_SCORES
WITH
tables_to_score AS (

-- ============================================================
-- INSURANCE AI HUB (E.D.I.E.) - Data Exploration Queries
-- Understand the structure, relationships, and patterns
-- ============================================================

USE DATABASE INSURANCE_AI_HUB;
USE WAREHOUSE INSURANCE_AI_HUB_WH;

-- ============================================================
-- 1. FULL INVENTORY: All tables with row counts and columns
-- ============================================================
SELECT
    TABLE_SCHEMA,
    TABLE_NAME,
    ROW_COUNT,
    COLUMN_COUNT,
    BYTES / 1024 / 1024 AS SIZE_MB,
    COMMENT
FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES
WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA IN ('ANALYTICS','DOCUMENTS','DATA_QUALITY')
ORDER BY TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME;

-- ============================================================
-- 2. COLUMN DETAILS: All 149 columns with types
-- ============================================================
SELECT
    TABLE_SCHEMA,
    TABLE_NAME,
    ORDINAL_POSITION,
    COLUMN_NAME,
    DATA_TYPE,
    IS_NULLABLE,
    COLUMN_DEFAULT
FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS
WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA IN ('ANALYTICS','DOCUMENTS','DATA_QUALITY')
ORDER BY TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME, ORDINAL_POSITION;

-- ============================================================
-- 3. CUSTOMERS - Sample & Distribution
-- ============================================================
SELECT * FROM ANALYTICS.CUSTOMERS LIMIT 10;

SELECT RISK_TIER, COUNT(*) AS CNT, ROUND(AVG(CREDIT_SCORE)) AS AVG_CREDIT
FROM ANALYTICS.CUSTOMERS GROUP BY RISK_TIER ORDER BY CNT DESC;

SELECT SEGMENT, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM ANALYTICS.CUSTOMERS GROUP BY SEGMENT ORDER BY CNT DESC;

SELECT STATE, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM ANALYTICS.CUSTOMERS GROUP BY STATE ORDER BY CNT DESC LIMIT 10;

SELECT
    'Null Emails' AS METRIC, COUNT(*) AS VALUE FROM ANALYTICS.CUSTOMERS WHERE EMAIL IS NULL
UNION ALL SELECT 'Null Phones', COUNT(*) FROM ANALYTICS.CUSTOMERS WHERE PHONE IS NULL
UNION ALL SELECT 'Duplicate Names', COUNT(*) FROM ANALYTICS.CUSTOMERS WHERE CUSTOMER_ID LIKE 'CUST-D%';

-- ============================================================
-- 4. AGENTS - Sample & Distribution
-- ============================================================
SELECT * FROM ANALYTICS.AGENTS LIMIT 10;

SELECT REGION, COUNT(*) AS CNT, ROUND(AVG(PERFORMANCE_RATING), 2) AS AVG_RATING
FROM ANALYTICS.AGENTS GROUP BY REGION ORDER BY CNT DESC;

SELECT SPECIALIZATION, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM ANALYTICS.AGENTS GROUP BY SPECIALIZATION ORDER BY CNT DESC;

SELECT STATUS, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM ANALYTICS.AGENTS GROUP BY STATUS;

-- Low performers with high policy counts (injected anomaly)
SELECT AGENT_ID, AGENT_NAME, REGION, PERFORMANCE_RATING, ACTIVE_POLICIES_COUNT
FROM ANALYTICS.AGENTS
WHERE PERFORMANCE_RATING < 2.0 AND ACTIVE_POLICIES_COUNT > 75
ORDER BY PERFORMANCE_RATING;

-- ============================================================
-- 5. POLICIES - Sample & Distribution
-- ============================================================
SELECT * FROM ANALYTICS.POLICIES LIMIT 10;

SELECT POLICY_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS CNT, ROUND(AVG(PREMIUM_AMOUNT), 2) AS AVG_PREMIUM,
       ROUND(AVG(COVERAGE_AMOUNT), 0) AS AVG_COVERAGE
FROM ANALYTICS.POLICIES GROUP BY POLICY_TYPE ORDER BY CNT DESC;

SELECT PLAN_TIER, COUNT(*) AS CNT, ROUND(AVG(DEDUCTIBLE), 2) AS AVG_DEDUCTIBLE
FROM ANALYTICS.POLICIES GROUP BY PLAN_TIER ORDER BY CNT DESC;

SELECT STATUS, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM ANALYTICS.POLICIES GROUP BY STATUS ORDER BY CNT DESC;

SELECT RENEWAL_STATUS, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM ANALYTICS.POLICIES GROUP BY RENEWAL_STATUS ORDER BY CNT DESC;

-- Premium outliers (injected)
SELECT POLICY_ID, POLICY_TYPE, PREMIUM_AMOUNT, COVERAGE_AMOUNT
FROM ANALYTICS.POLICIES WHERE PREMIUM_AMOUNT > 10000 ORDER BY PREMIUM_AMOUNT DESC;

-- ============================================================
-- 6. CLAIMS - Sample & Distribution
-- ============================================================
SELECT * FROM ANALYTICS.CLAIMS LIMIT 10;

SELECT CLAIM_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS CNT, ROUND(AVG(CLAIM_AMOUNT), 2) AS AVG_AMOUNT,
       ROUND(AVG(FRAUD_SCORE), 2) AS AVG_FRAUD
FROM ANALYTICS.CLAIMS GROUP BY CLAIM_TYPE ORDER BY CNT DESC;

SELECT STATUS, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM ANALYTICS.CLAIMS GROUP BY STATUS ORDER BY CNT DESC;

-- Seasonal distribution (monthly)
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', CLAIM_DATE) AS MONTH, COUNT(*) AS CLAIMS
FROM ANALYTICS.CLAIMS GROUP BY MONTH ORDER BY MONTH;

-- Fraud score distribution
SELECT
    CASE
        WHEN FRAUD_SCORE < 20 THEN '0-20 (Low)'
        WHEN FRAUD_SCORE < 40 THEN '20-40 (Normal)'
        WHEN FRAUD_SCORE < 60 THEN '40-60 (Elevated)'
        WHEN FRAUD_SCORE < 80 THEN '60-80 (High)'
        ELSE '80-100 (Critical)'
    END AS FRAUD_BAND,
    COUNT(*) AS CNT
FROM ANALYTICS.CLAIMS GROUP BY FRAUD_BAND ORDER BY FRAUD_BAND;

-- Resolution days distribution
SELECT
    CASE
        WHEN RESOLUTION_DAYS <= 30 THEN '0-30 days'
        WHEN RESOLUTION_DAYS <= 90 THEN '31-90 days'
        WHEN RESOLUTION_DAYS <= 180 THEN '91-180 days'
        ELSE '180+ days'
    END AS RESOLUTION_BAND,
    COUNT(*) AS CNT, ROUND(AVG(FRICTION_SCORE), 2) AS AVG_FRICTION
FROM ANALYTICS.CLAIMS GROUP BY RESOLUTION_BAND ORDER BY RESOLUTION_BAND;

-- Hurricane claims (injected seasonal spike)
SELECT CAUSE_OF_LOSS, COUNT(*) AS CNT, ROUND(AVG(CLAIM_AMOUNT), 2) AS AVG_AMT
FROM ANALYTICS.CLAIMS
WHERE CAUSE_OF_LOSS = 'Hurricane/Tropical Storm'
GROUP BY CAUSE_OF_LOSS;

-- ============================================================
-- 7. BILLING - Sample & Distribution
-- ============================================================
SELECT * FROM ANALYTICS.BILLING LIMIT 10;

SELECT PAYMENT_STATUS, COUNT(*) AS CNT,
       ROUND(SUM(OUTSTANDING_BALANCE), 2) AS TOTAL_OUTSTANDING,
       ROUND(SUM(LATE_FEE), 2) AS TOTAL_LATE_FEES
FROM ANALYTICS.BILLING GROUP BY PAYMENT_STATUS ORDER BY CNT DESC;

SELECT PAYMENT_METHOD, COUNT(*) AS CNT
FROM ANALYTICS.BILLING WHERE PAYMENT_METHOD IS NOT NULL GROUP BY PAYMENT_METHOD ORDER BY CNT DESC;

-- Delinquency rate by month
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', INVOICE_DATE) AS MONTH,
       COUNT(*) AS TOTAL_INVOICES,
       SUM(CASE WHEN PAYMENT_STATUS = 'Overdue' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS OVERDUE,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN PAYMENT_STATUS = 'Overdue' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS OVERDUE_PCT
FROM ANALYTICS.BILLING GROUP BY MONTH ORDER BY MONTH DESC LIMIT 12;

-- ============================================================
-- 8. AT_RISK_POLICIES - Sample & Distribution
-- ============================================================
SELECT * FROM ANALYTICS.AT_RISK_POLICIES LIMIT 10;

SELECT RISK_CATEGORY, COUNT(*) AS CNT,
       ROUND(AVG(CHURN_PROBABILITY), 4) AS AVG_CHURN_PROB,
       ROUND(SUM(REVENUE_AT_RISK), 2) AS TOTAL_REVENUE_AT_RISK
FROM ANALYTICS.AT_RISK_POLICIES GROUP BY RISK_CATEGORY ORDER BY TOTAL_REVENUE_AT_RISK DESC;

SELECT RETENTION_ACTION, COUNT(*) AS CNT
FROM ANALYTICS.AT_RISK_POLICIES GROUP BY RETENTION_ACTION ORDER BY CNT DESC;

-- High churn + high revenue at risk (top 10)
SELECT RISK_ID, POLICY_ID, CUSTOMER_ID, CHURN_PROBABILITY, REVENUE_AT_RISK, MISSED_PAYMENTS_COUNT, NPS_SCORE
FROM ANALYTICS.AT_RISK_POLICIES
ORDER BY CHURN_PROBABILITY * REVENUE_AT_RISK DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- ============================================================
-- 9. POLICY_DOCUMENTS - Sample & Content Preview
-- ============================================================
SELECT DOCUMENT_ID, POLICY_ID, DOCUMENT_TYPE, TITLE, LEFT(CONTENT, 200) AS CONTENT_PREVIEW,
       SUMMARY, EFFECTIVE_DATE, VERSION, FILE_FORMAT
FROM DOCUMENTS.POLICY_DOCUMENTS LIMIT 10;

SELECT DOCUMENT_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM DOCUMENTS.POLICY_DOCUMENTS GROUP BY DOCUMENT_TYPE ORDER BY CNT DESC;

-- ============================================================
-- 10. DOCUMENT_CHUNKS - RAG Layer Preview
-- ============================================================
SELECT CHUNK_ID, DOCUMENT_ID, CHUNK_INDEX, LEFT(CHUNK_TEXT, 150) AS CHUNK_PREVIEW, TOKEN_COUNT, EMBEDDING_MODEL
FROM DOCUMENTS.DOCUMENT_CHUNKS LIMIT 10;

SELECT EMBEDDING_MODEL, COUNT(*) AS CNT, ROUND(AVG(TOKEN_COUNT)) AS AVG_TOKENS
FROM DOCUMENTS.DOCUMENT_CHUNKS GROUP BY EMBEDDING_MODEL;

-- ============================================================
-- 11. DQ_RULES - All 50 Rules Overview
-- ============================================================
SELECT * FROM DATA_QUALITY.DQ_RULES ORDER BY RULE_ID;

SELECT RULE_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM DATA_QUALITY.DQ_RULES GROUP BY RULE_TYPE ORDER BY CNT DESC;

SELECT TARGET_TABLE, COUNT(*) AS RULES_COUNT FROM DATA_QUALITY.DQ_RULES GROUP BY TARGET_TABLE ORDER BY RULES_COUNT DESC;

SELECT SEVERITY, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM DATA_QUALITY.DQ_RULES GROUP BY SEVERITY ORDER BY CNT DESC;

-- ============================================================
-- 12. DQ_RESULTS - Execution History
-- ============================================================
SELECT * FROM DATA_QUALITY.DQ_RESULTS ORDER BY RUN_DATE DESC LIMIT 10;

SELECT STATUS, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM DATA_QUALITY.DQ_RESULTS GROUP BY STATUS ORDER BY CNT DESC;

-- Rules that fail most often
SELECT r.RULE_NAME, r.TARGET_TABLE, r.SEVERITY, COUNT(*) AS FAIL_COUNT
FROM DATA_QUALITY.DQ_RESULTS res
JOIN DATA_QUALITY.DQ_RULES r ON res.RULE_ID = r.RULE_ID
WHERE res.STATUS = 'Fail'
GROUP BY r.RULE_NAME, r.TARGET_TABLE, r.SEVERITY
ORDER BY FAIL_COUNT DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- ============================================================
-- 13. DQ_SCORES - Table Health Over Time
-- ============================================================
SELECT * FROM DATA_QUALITY.DQ_SCORES ORDER BY SCORE_DATE DESC LIMIT 10;

-- Latest score per table
SELECT TABLE_NAME, OVERALL_SCORE, COMPLETENESS_SCORE, VALIDITY_SCORE, TIMELINESS_SCORE, TREND, SCORE_DATE
FROM DATA_QUALITY.DQ_SCORES
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY TABLE_NAME ORDER BY SCORE_DATE DESC) = 1
ORDER BY OVERALL_SCORE;

-- ============================================================
-- 14. DQ_COLUMN_HEALTH - Column-Level Issues
-- ============================================================
SELECT * FROM DATA_QUALITY.DQ_COLUMN_HEALTH ORDER BY CHECK_DATE DESC LIMIT 10;

-- Unhealthiest columns
SELECT TABLE_NAME, COLUMN_NAME, ROUND(AVG(HEALTH_SCORE), 2) AS AVG_HEALTH,
       ROUND(AVG(NULL_RATE), 2) AS AVG_NULL_RATE,
       ROUND(AVG(OUTLIER_RATE), 2) AS AVG_OUTLIER_RATE,
       MAX(STATUS) AS WORST_STATUS
FROM DATA_QUALITY.DQ_COLUMN_HEALTH
GROUP BY TABLE_NAME, COLUMN_NAME
ORDER BY AVG_HEALTH
LIMIT 15;

-- ============================================================
-- 15. CROSS-TABLE ANALYTICS (Join Queries)
-- ============================================================

-- Customer 360: Full customer view with policies, claims, billing
SELECT
    c.CUSTOMER_ID, c.FIRST_NAME || ' ' || c.LAST_NAME AS FULL_NAME,
    c.RISK_TIER, c.CREDIT_SCORE, c.SEGMENT,
    COUNT(DISTINCT p.POLICY_ID) AS POLICY_COUNT,
    COUNT(DISTINCT cl.CLAIM_ID) AS CLAIM_COUNT,
    ROUND(SUM(DISTINCT p.PREMIUM_AMOUNT), 2) AS TOTAL_PREMIUMS,
    ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(b.OUTSTANDING_BALANCE), 0), 2) AS TOTAL_OUTSTANDING
FROM ANALYTICS.CUSTOMERS c
LEFT JOIN ANALYTICS.POLICIES p ON c.CUSTOMER_ID = p.CUSTOMER_ID
LEFT JOIN ANALYTICS.CLAIMS cl ON c.CUSTOMER_ID = cl.CUSTOMER_ID
LEFT JOIN ANALYTICS.BILLING b ON c.CUSTOMER_ID = b.CUSTOMER_ID AND b.PAYMENT_STATUS = 'Overdue'
GROUP BY c.CUSTOMER_ID, FULL_NAME, c.RISK_TIER, c.CREDIT_SCORE, c.SEGMENT
ORDER BY TOTAL_OUTSTANDING DESC
LIMIT 20;

-- Agent Performance: Claims + Policies + Risk
SELECT
    a.AGENT_ID, a.AGENT_NAME, a.REGION, a.SPECIALIZATION, a.PERFORMANCE_RATING,
    COUNT(DISTINCT p.POLICY_ID) AS POLICIES_MANAGED,
    COUNT(DISTINCT cl.CLAIM_ID) AS CLAIMS_ON_POLICIES,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ar.RISK_ID) AS AT_RISK_COUNT,
    ROUND(SUM(ar.REVENUE_AT_RISK), 2) AS TOTAL_REVENUE_AT_RISK
FROM ANALYTICS.AGENTS a
LEFT JOIN ANALYTICS.POLICIES p ON a.AGENT_ID = p.AGENT_ID
LEFT JOIN ANALYTICS.CLAIMS cl ON p.POLICY_ID = cl.POLICY_ID
LEFT JOIN ANALYTICS.AT_RISK_POLICIES ar ON p.POLICY_ID = ar.POLICY_ID
GROUP BY a.AGENT_ID, a.AGENT_NAME, a.REGION, a.SPECIALIZATION, a.PERFORMANCE_RATING
ORDER BY TOTAL_REVENUE_AT_RISK DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 20;

-- Claims by Region (for the "North Region spike" demo)
SELECT
    a.REGION,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', cl.CLAIM_DATE) AS MONTH,
    COUNT(*) AS CLAIM_COUNT,
    ROUND(SUM(cl.CLAIM_AMOUNT), 2) AS TOTAL_CLAIMED,
    ROUND(AVG(cl.FRAUD_SCORE), 2) AS AVG_FRAUD_SCORE
FROM ANALYTICS.CLAIMS cl
JOIN ANALYTICS.POLICIES p ON cl.POLICY_ID = p.POLICY_ID
JOIN ANALYTICS.AGENTS a ON p.AGENT_ID = a.AGENT_ID
WHERE cl.CLAIM_DATE >= '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY a.REGION, MONTH
ORDER BY a.REGION, MONTH;

-- Revenue at Risk by Policy Type
SELECT
    p.POLICY_TYPE,
    COUNT(*) AS AT_RISK_COUNT,
    ROUND(SUM(ar.REVENUE_AT_RISK), 2) AS TOTAL_REVENUE_AT_RISK,
    ROUND(AVG(ar.CHURN_PROBABILITY), 4) AS AVG_CHURN_PROB,
    ROUND(AVG(ar.MISSED_PAYMENTS_COUNT), 1) AS AVG_MISSED_PAYMENTS
FROM ANALYTICS.AT_RISK_POLICIES ar
JOIN ANALYTICS.POLICIES p ON ar.POLICY_ID = p.POLICY_ID
GROUP BY p.POLICY_TYPE
ORDER BY TOTAL_REVENUE_AT_RISK DESC;

name: sql-author
description: "Use for ANY task that writes, fixes, runs, or debugs Snowflake SQL. Especially use when the user provides a failed query, a Snowflake SQL error, asks to repair SQL, asks for data from tables/views, or needs query validation."

# SQL Author

Write or fix Snowflake SQL by grounding the answer in the actual schema and by validating the final statement before presenting it.

## Workflow

1. **Read the full request and failed SQL first.** Identify the user goal, the failing statement, the Snowflake error, and whether the task is a fix, a new query, or an investigation. Many failed fixes come from solving only the visible syntax error while missing the query's intended shape.

2. **Inspect real objects before changing columns or joins.** Use `DESCRIBE TABLE`, `SHOW TABLES`, `SHOW VIEWS`, or `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS` because Snowflake errors such as invalid identifier, ambiguous column, type mismatch, and object-not-found often require knowing the real column names and types. Guessing column names is faster but commonly creates a new compile error.

3. **Check table size.** Query `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES` for `ROW_COUNT` before running against unfamiliar tables. Add date/partition filters to avoid long query time. Tell the user: which table, what date range, what filters, how you're computing the metric. If any of these feel like guesses, stop and ask — a one-turn clarification beats a confident wrong answer.

4. **Use object search when the object is incomplete or ambiguous.** If the user gives a partial table name or the SQL references an object that may be a view, use `cortex search object "<name>"` before declaring it missing. Ask the user only when multiple plausible objects remain. For complex SQL, try `cortex semantic-views search "<topic>"`. Semantic views have verified metric definitions.

5. **Check unfamiliar Snowflake syntax and functions.** Use `cortex search docs "<function or syntax>"` or a tiny compile-only probe when you are not certain. Snowflake has sharp dialect rules around `QUALIFY`, `LATERAL FLATTEN`, recursive CTEs, `OBJECT_AGG`, `ARRAY_CAT`, `TRY_CAST`, `TYPEOF`, stage syntax, and `INFORMATION_SCHEMA` table functions.

6. **Fix the root cause, not just the first parser error.** Syntax cleanup can reveal deeper errors such as nested aggregates, wrong CTE scope, bad aliases, invalid casts, or unsupported correlated subqueries. After each change, reconsider whether the new SQL still satisfies the original user intent.

7. **Prefer conservative rewrites.** Preserve selected columns, filters, grouping grain, ordering, and limits unless they are the reason the query fails. A compiling query that changes the result shape is not a good fix.

8. **Handle common Snowflake gotchas deliberately.**
   - `!= 'value'` does not match NULLs; include `OR col IS NULL` when that is intended.
   - `COUNT(col)` excludes NULLs; `COUNT(*)` does not.
   - Use `QUALIFY` for window filters instead of wrapping when possible.
   - Use `ILIKE` instead of `LOWER(col) LIKE` for case-insensitive filters.
   - Use `DIV0NULL` or `NULLIF` for division safety.
   - Cast `VARIANT` fields explicitly before comparison or aggregation.
   - `ARRAY_CAT` takes two arrays; nest calls for more than two.

9. **Diagnose access errors instead of rewriting blindly.** When the error is privilege-related, run `CALL EXPLAIN_PRIVILEGES(statement => '<failing_sql>', missing_only => true, for_role => '<role>')`. SQL-authoring cannot fix a missing grant, but the user still needs a precise explanation.

10. **Validate the exact final SQL.** Before presenting the SQL to the user, call `snowflake_sql_execute` with `only_compile=true` on the complete final statement. Compile-only validation is cheap and catches the exact failure class this skill is meant to prevent: syntax errors, invalid identifiers, bad function signatures, and type mismatches. If validation fails, read the new error, revise the SQL, and validate again. Keep validating and fix the SQL to be presented until it passes the compile with no error.

# E.D.I.E. — Enterprise Data & Intelligence Engine

## Insurance AI Hub

> A trusted, AI-enabled insurance data platform that gives the business a 360° view of customers and policies, helps manage claims and revenue, identifies risk, answers questions from policy documents, and continuously monitors data quality.

---

## What is E.D.I.E.?

**EDIE** (Enterprise Data & Intelligence Engine) is an AI-enabled insurance data platform that brings together customer, policy, claims, billing, risk, documents, and data-quality information to provide trusted insights and intelligent decision support.

| Word | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Enterprise** | Broad enough for the whole insurance organization |
| **Data** | Represents the integrated insurance data foundation |
| **Intelligence** | Covers analytics, AI, RAG and insights |
| **Engine** | Positions EDIE as a platform that powers multiple use cases |

---

## Architecture

```
                         INSURANCE AI HUB
                               │
              ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐
              │                │                │
         ANALYTICS        DOCUMENTS       DATA_QUALITY
              │                │                │
    ┌─────────┼─────────┐   ┌─┴──┐      ┌─────┼──────┐
    │    │    │    │     │   │    │      │     │      │
 CUST  AGT  POL  CLM  BILL DOCS CHUNKS RULES SCORES RESULTS
                   │                                   │
              AT_RISK                            COL_HEALTH
```

### Three Pillars (Track 6 Alignment)

| Pillar | Schema | Cortex Solution |
|--------|--------|-----------------|
| Self-Service Analytics | `ANALYTICS` | Cortex Analyst + Semantic View |
| Document Intelligence & RAG | `DOCUMENTS` | Cortex Search |
| Data Trust & Observability | `DATA_QUALITY` | Conversational DQ Agent |

---

## Database Inventory

| Schema | Table | Rows | Type | Purpose |
|--------|-------|------|------|---------|
| ANALYTICS | CUSTOMERS | 5,015 | Dimension | Customer profiles, demographics, risk tiers |
| ANALYTICS | AGENTS | 150 | Dimension | Agent profiles, regions, performance |
| ANALYTICS | POLICIES | 8,000 | Fact | Policy coverage, premiums, status |
| ANALYTICS | CLAIMS | 3,562 | Fact | Claims, fraud scores, resolution |
| ANALYTICS | BILLING | 20,000 | Fact | Invoices, payments, balances |
| ANALYTICS | AT_RISK_POLICIES | 1,200 | Snapshot | Churn probability, revenue at risk |
| DOCUMENTS | POLICY_DOCUMENTS | 2,000 | Document | Full policy contract text |
| DOCUMENTS | DOCUMENT_CHUNKS | 12,000 | RAG | Chunked text for vector search |
| DATA_QUALITY | DQ_RULES | 50 | Config | DQ rule definitions |
| DATA_QUALITY | DQ_RESULTS | 5,000 | Execution | Rule pass/fail history |
| DATA_QUALITY | DQ_SCORES | 1,000 | Scores | Table-level quality scores |
| DATA_QUALITY | DQ_COLUMN_HEALTH | 3,000 | Health | Column-level null/outlier metrics |

**Total: 12 tables, 149 columns, ~61,000 rows**

---

# Streamlit in Snowflake — Workspace apps (new and existing)

**NEW APP CREATION MODE:** **create** a **new** app in an **empty** dedicated folder (first-level under the Workspace root); run preflight and **`read references/workspace-session-and-defaults.md`** before the first **`snowflake.yml`** write.

**EDIT MODE:** change an **existing** project (same **`read references/streamlit-in-snowflake-runtime.md`** gate before writes). Use **`read references/workspace-session-and-defaults.md`** when the work touches **role**, **compute pool**, **query warehouse**, or repairing **App Settings** / broken resource alignment—not for trivial UI-only edits with no session context.

## REQUIRED documentation (read first, every time)

**Before any `write` to app files** (**creating** a new app **or** **editing** an existing app), **`read references/streamlit-in-snowflake-runtime.md`**. This file is **mandatory** for every task in this skill: it explains how hosted Snowflake differs from laptop Streamlit for **secrets vs embedded identity**, **PyPI / external access integrations**, and **which files exist at runtime** (`artifacts`, uploads, static assets). Treat it as a gate—do not skip it in the same session before changing Python, YAML, or config in the user’s project.

**NEW APP CREATION MODE — second mandatory read:** **`read references/workspace-session-and-defaults.md`** before the first **`snowflake.yml`** `write` (from **`default_template/`**) and before advising **role**, **compute pool**, or **query warehouse** (**`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** only) in **Workspace / App Settings**. Run the SQL in that file when the host supports it. Do not skip for new apps—even if the user never mentions warehouse or pool. **If there is no Snowflake SQL session** (or **`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** is null), that file still **must** be read once; then follow its **exception path for creating the project without a resolvable session warehouse** (see **`references/workspace-session-and-defaults.md`**, section 2): **`write`** minimal **`snowflake.yml`** with **`query_warehouse`** and **`compute_pool`** **omitted** (no **`<...>`** placeholders), not a hard stop before any **`write`**.

**SCOPE:** **NEW APP CREATION MODE** creates a **new** app in an empty folder; **EDIT MODE** updates an existing app (including repairing **`snowflake.yml`** or App Settings that were set up incorrectly when the app was first created). Covers project files, minimal `snowflake.yml` (including **`main_file`** aligned with the entry script), `pyproject.toml`, `.streamlit/config.toml`, the Streamlit entry **`.py`** file (default name **`streamlit_app.py`**), dependency and EAI guidance, and Run/preview instructions.

**ENVIRONMENT:** Snowsight Workspace IDE (browser-based). Files are created or updated using the `write` tool with `file_path` and `content` parameters (and `read` to inspect existing sources).

**Python version:** Workspace Streamlit in this product path supports **Python 3.11 only**. Keep **`requires-python`** and any runtime expectations aligned with **3.11** (see **`default_template/pyproject.toml`**); do not target other Python versions for hosted runs.

**DO NOT use this skill when:**
- The user is working in **regular Snowflake worksheets** (SQL worksheets), not a Streamlit app project
- The user explicitly wants a **warehouse-based** Streamlit app outside the Workspace / container product surface this skill targets

## Tools

Use the file and discovery tools the host provides (names may vary slightly by product; align with the **ENVIRONMENT** line above).

| Action | Tool | Notes |
|--------|------|--------|
| Load skill references and app source | **`read`** | **`references/streamlit-in-snowflake-runtime.md`** before writes (every task). **NEW APP CREATION MODE:** **`references/workspace-session-and-defaults.md`** before first **`snowflake.yml`** write and before role / pool / warehouse guidance (see **REQUIRED documentation**). Then **`read`** files you edit; other **`references/*.md`** per routing. |
| Create or update app files | **`write`** | Project files only under the app folder; keep **`main_file`** and **`artifacts`** consistent. |

## Error handling

**If `read` / `list_dir` / `write` fails** (path not found, permission denied, empty or unreadable `snowflake.yml`, repeated failures on the same path):

1. **Re-check the path** — use **absolute** paths the user or Workspace shows; confirm the app folder and filenames (typos, wrong branch or repo).
2. **Assume a Workspace / Snowsight issue when appropriate** — the file tree may not be synced, the project may not be open, or the product may be temporarily unable to read that path. Tell the user clearly: *this may be a **Snowflake Workspace** or **Snowsight** issue* (not only a bug in the app code). Suggest: refresh the Workspace, confirm the correct **project** and **repository** are open, try again after a short wait, or contact an **org admin** if access or the Container Runtime is misconfigured.
3. **Do not** keep retrying the same failing tool call in a loop without new information; after one or two attempts, **stop** and report the error and the Workspace-oriented guidance above.

### Step 2: Apply changes

#### NEW APP CREATION MODE — Create new app

**Goal:** Create a **new empty** project folder (kebab-case slug) with required files.

**Where it lives:** The project is always a **dedicated directory at the Workspace tree root**—a **direct child** of the Workspace file root (a **first-level folder** next to any other projects), with all app files **inside** that folder. **Do not** drop `snowflake.yml` / `pyproject.toml` loose at the Workspace root with no folder. **Do not** create a second app **inside** another Streamlit project directory (see **No nesting** below).

```
<project-folder>/
├── .streamlit/
│   └── config.toml
├── pyproject.toml
├── snowflake.yml   # main_file: <entry>.py (default streamlit_app.py)
└── streamlit_app.py   # or another name if main_file matches

## Code Restrictions

- Use `st.connection("snowflake", ttl=os.getenv("SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTION_TTL"))` and `import os`; `.session()` for Snowpark when needed.
- Do NOT use `from snowflake.snowpark.context import get_active_session`.
- Do NOT use `snowflake.connector` directly or hard-code credentials.
- Do NOT use `env_var()` or environment variables for **authentication**.

### SQL injection (mandatory for dynamic SQL)

- **Values** (literals from widgets, chat, `st.text_input`, etc.): never build SQL with **f-strings**, string **`+`**, or **`.format()`**. Use `conn.query(sql, params=...)` or `session.sql(..., params=...)` with bound parameters. **`read references/snowflake-connection.md`** before writing dynamic queries.
- **Identifiers** (database, schema, table, or column **names** that change by user choice): query bind parameters are for **values**, not arbitrary identifiers. Use a fixed **allowlist** (e.g. dict mapping user-facing labels to known `IDENTIFIER`s) or a small set of **predefined SQL** branches—never `f"SELECT {user_column} FROM ..."` with unconstrained `user_column`.

## Runtime Settings

App Settings can change DB, schema, warehouse, and compute pool after creation (**NEW APP CREATION MODE** resource alignment: **REQUIRED documentation**, **Required Files §1**).

## External access integrations (EAI) and PyPI

EAIs are account-specific; do not assume fixed integration names.

**Docs:** [External access overview](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/external-network-access/external-network-access-overview), [Streamlit dependencies](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/streamlit/app-development/dependency-management).

**Extra PyPI packages:** User attaches PyPI-capable EAI in App Settings before `pyproject.toml` changes that pull new wheels.

- **Step 1**: Vague request → ask before editing
- **NEW APP CREATION MODE**: Target is non-empty, already a Streamlit app root, or nested under another app root → **stop**; use edit mode, a new **sibling** folder, or ask the user to name an empty path
- **Step 3**: Always tell user to click Run; never auto-launch

## Troubleshooting

- **Fails after creating or editing the app:** Ask the user to click **Run** again; confirm **`snowflake.yml`** matches minimal Workspace rules (including resolved **`query_warehouse`** / **`compute_pool`** or keys removed for App Settings).
- **Wrong app runs or “file not found” after renaming:** Confirm **`main_file`** matches the entry **`.py`** on disk and **`artifacts`** lists that path.
- **Failed to retrieve packages:** Unmodified default `pyproject.toml` unless EAI is set up.
- **Connection errors:** **`read references/workspace-session-and-defaults.md`** — confirm **`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** is set (else **Workspace settings**); verify primary role; **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`** then **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** and **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`**; confirm **`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** appears in the warehouse **`SHOW`** output; then check `st.connection("snowflake", ttl=os.getenv("SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTION_TTL"))`.
- **New app creation overwrote or nested inside another app:** Preflight failed—restore from version control if needed; use an **empty sibling** project folder and NEW APP CREATION MODE, or **EDIT MODE** to edit the existing app.

Let me read the required reference files before creating the Streamlit app.

1... # Workspace Streamlit — session role, defaults, and access checks
2... 
3... Use this reference when you must **discover or validate** the Snowflake context around a Workspace Streamlit app: **active role**, **account default Streamlit compute pool**, and the **session query warehouse** (**`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** only)—so App Settings / non-minimal `snowflake.yml` (or user guidance) matches what the account and session actually provide.
4... 
5... **Scope:** SQL you run in the **user’s Snowflake session** (Snowsight worksheet, SQL workspace, or any connection that mirrors their UI role). This file is **self-contained**; do not rely on other Cortex skills to perform these steps.
6... 
7... **`default_template/snowflake.yml`** may use **`<QUERY_WAREHOUSE>`** / **`<COMPUTE_POOL>`**—after preflight, substitute from **`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** and the pool **`SHOW`** below (or a pool the user confirms from that list), **or delete** both keys for App Settings only; never leave unresolved `<...>` in **`snowflake.yml`** (or other files you write). Use this doc to preflight and align settings; do not add **`identifier`**, **`runtime_name`**, or **`external_access_integrations`** unless the user leaves the minimal Workspace path.
8... 
9... ---
10... 
11... ## 1. What to collect (two layers)
12... 
13... | Layer | What it answers | Typical use |
14... |-------|-----------------|-------------|
15... | **Session** | Active role and **query warehouse** | `CURRENT_ROLE()`, **`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** — the only source for query warehouse in this workflow |
16... | **Account object parameters** | Account-wide Streamlit **compute pool** default | **`DEFAULT_STREAMLIT_COMPUTE_POOL`** |
17... 
18... ---
19... 
20... ## 2. Session — primary role and query warehouse
21... 
22... Run as the user (same connection as Snowsight / Workspace when possible):
23... 
24... ```sql
25... SELECT
26...   CURRENT_ROLE()      AS primary_role,
27...   CURRENT_WAREHOUSE() AS active_warehouse;
28... ```
29... 
30... **Query warehouse:** Use **`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** only. If it returns **NULL** or an empty string, **do not** infer a warehouse from other parameters or fabricate a name for preflight.
31... 
32... **Stopping point — no warehouse in session (narrow):** Tell the user to set a **query / default warehouse** in **Workspace settings** (Snowsight Workspace configuration for the project or connection—wherever this product exposes warehouse selection), then **`SELECT CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** again when they can run SQL. **Do not** substitute invented warehouse or pool names in `snowflake.yml`, and **do not** run **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** (or pick a **`query_warehouse`**) as if a warehouse were already resolved while **`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** is still null.
33... 
34... **Exception — create without resolvable session resources:** When **`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** is null **or** this environment cannot run Snowflake SQL (no session, headless agent, file-only workflow), you may still **`write`** project files when **creating a new app** after **`read`** this file: use **`default_template/snowflake.yml`**, **remove** both **`query_warehouse`** and **`compute_pool`** keys (App Settings / Workspace UI will supply them), and ensure there are **no** unresolved **`<...>`** placeholders. Tell the user they must set warehouse and compute pool in **App Settings** (or Workspace) before **Run** succeeds. This path is normal for minimal apps and automated setups that only create project files. When SQL **does** run but **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** or **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** returns **no rows**, use the **same** key removal and user messaging—see **sections 4–5** and **Omit both keys** (later in **section 2**, after **Restricted sessions**).
35... 
36... **Primary role:** `CURRENT_ROLE()` is the **primary** role for the session. Workspace and Streamlit permission checks should be reasoned about for this role.
37... 
38... **Warehouse listing (section 5):** Run **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`** immediately before **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** **when the session allows it**, so the listing reflects **primary-role** warehouse access once secondary roles are cleared. If **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`** fails with a **restricted-session** error (see below), run **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** without **`USE`** and treat the output as the fixed-session listing. For **other** `USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE` failures on this path, warehouse preflight may be inconclusive—capture the error for the user and **do not** treat **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** as a **primary-role-only** allowlist until **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`** succeeds and you re-run **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`**, or the user confirms warehouse access another way.
39... 
40... **Compute pools (section 4):** Use **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** only. Optionally run **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`** first **when the session allows it**; if **`USE`** hits a **restricted-session** error, run **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** without **`USE`**.
41... 
42... ### Restricted sessions — “Current session is restricted”
43... 
44... Some connections (including many **automation / agent** SQL sessions) reject role-changing statements. If **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`** returns an error whose text indicates the session is **restricted**—for example **`Current session is restricted`** together with **`USE ROLE not allowed`** (or similar wording from your Snowflake build)—**interpret that as: secondary roles are already in a fixed state for this session** (you cannot toggle them from this tool; they are effectively **not** being applied in a way you can change here). That is **not** the same as “no SQL session” and **not**, by itself, a reason to skip **sections 4–5** discovery (**`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`**, **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`**).
45... 
46... **What to do:** **Omit** the **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`** line and run **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** and **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** as in **sections 4–5**. Treat **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** as the warehouse listing for this workflow ( **`USAGE`**-relevant rows; see **section 5**); treat **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** as the account pool catalog for real pool names. **Do not** skip those **`SHOW`s** when this reference expects them, or invent **`query_warehouse`** instead of following **sections 4–6**. **Do not** use the **section 2** “omit **`query_warehouse`** / **`compute_pool`**” creation exception **only** because **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`** failed with this restricted pattern—when **`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** is non-null and the **`SHOW`s succeed**, still substitute real names from **`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** and from **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** per **sections 4–6** **when those listings are non-empty**. **Do not** invent **`query_warehouse`** or **`compute_pool`** when the relevant **`SHOW`** returns **no rows**—use the **stopping points** in **sections 4–5** (prompt the user; **new app** omit flow below).
47... 
48... **Omit both keys (same pattern as warehouses):** When you **cannot** place a real **`query_warehouse`** and **`compute_pool`** from this reference (**`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** null per **section 2**, **no rows** from **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** per **section 5**, or **no rows** from **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** per **section 4**), **remove** both keys from **`snowflake.yml`**, ensure **no** unresolved **`<...>`** placeholders, and tell the user **App Settings** (or Workspace) must supply warehouse and compute pool before **Run** succeeds—same user-facing outcome as **section 2**’s creation exception.
49... 
50... ---
51... 
52... ## 3. Account default — Streamlit compute pool
53... 
54... Account-level **object parameters** (set with `ALTER ACCOUNT ... SET`) include a Streamlit-oriented **compute pool** default. Inspect it with `SHOW PARAMETERS` scoped to the account:
55... 
56... ```sql
57... SHOW PARAMETERS LIKE 'DEFAULT_STREAMLIT_COMPUTE_POOL' IN ACCOUNT;
58... ```
59... 
60... Interpretation:
61... 
62... - **`DEFAULT_STREAMLIT_COMPUTE_POOL`** — Account default **compute pool** name for Streamlit (and related) container workloads when the product does not override it elsewhere.
63... 
64... Read the **`value`** (or `default`) column from the result set. Empty or unset values mean there is **no account-wide compute pool default**; use **section 4** to list usable pools and pick a fallback with the user.
65... 
66... ---
67... 
68... ## 4. Compute pools — list pools in the account (mandatory)
69... 
70... Run **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** to list compute pools so you can align **`compute_pool`** in **`snowflake.yml`** with **`DEFAULT_STREAMLIT_COMPUTE_POOL`** (**section 3**) and pick a real pool name from the catalog.
71... 
72... When the session allows **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`**, you may run it before **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** for consistency with **section 5**; it is **optional** for pools: If you think it is available and it fails, do not treat that as a fatal error, continue execution.
73... 
74... ```sql
75... USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;
76... 
77... SHOW COMPUTE POOLS;
78... ```
79... 
80... **Restricted session:** If **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`** fails with **“Current session is restricted”** / **“USE ROLE not allowed”** (see **Restricted sessions** under **section 2**), **skip** the **`USE`** line and run **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS;`** alone.
81... 
82... **Why:** **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** is widely supported across Snowflake versions and SQL surfaces. Use it to check whether the account default pool (**section 3**) appears in the listing and to pick a fallback **from that listing** with the user.
83... 
84... **Validate the default:** After reading **`DEFAULT_STREAMLIT_COMPUTE_POOL`**, confirm that name appears in **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** (or run a filtered variant if your build supports it, e.g. `SHOW COMPUTE POOLS LIKE '<name>'`). If it does **not** appear, choose a pool from the **same** result set with the user or rely on **App Settings** (omit **`query_warehouse`** and **`compute_pool`** per **Omit both keys** in **section 2** when you emit **`snowflake.yml`** without a SQL-resolvable pool).
85... 
86... **No default or empty parameter:** Use only names returned by **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** when suggesting a pool from SQL; never invent names.
87... 
88... **Stopping point — no compute pools in the listing:** If **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** returns **no rows**, the session’s primary role has **no** pool in the catalog for this workflow—**do not** copy **`DEFAULT_STREAMLIT_COMPUTE_POOL`** (from **section 3**) or any other name into **`snowflake.yml`**. Tell the user they need **`USAGE` on COMPUTE POOL** (or equivalent access), a **different role**, or configuration in **App Settings** after an admin grants access, then re-run **section 4** when they can run SQL again. For **new-app creation `write`s**, **remove** both **`query_warehouse`** and **`compute_pool`**, ensure **no** unresolved **`<...>`**, and tell the user **App Settings** (or Workspace) must supply warehouse and compute pool before **Run** succeeds—the **same** prompt / omit pattern as **section 2** (no session warehouse) and as **section 5** (no warehouses with **`USAGE`**).
89... 
90... ---
91... 
92... ## 5. Warehouses — `USAGE` for the current primary role (mandatory)
93... 
94... Run the following **in order** when the session allows **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`**; treat the **`SHOW`** output as the **only** authoritative list of warehouses the **current primary role** may use with **`USAGE`** when secondary roles are cleared:
95... 
96... ```sql
97... USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;
98... 
99... SHOW WAREHOUSES;
100... ```
101... 
102... **Restricted session:** If **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`** fails with the **restricted-session** pattern (**section 2**), **skip** the **`USE`** line and run **`SHOW WAREHOUSES;`** alone.
103... 
104... **Why:** **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`** scopes to the primary role when permitted; in **restricted** sessions, assume **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** still reflects the **current primary role** for this fixed session. Use this result in **section 6** to confirm **`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** (from **section 2**) appears in the listing. **Compute pools** use **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** (**section 4**)—a different command shape.
105... 
106... **Filtered variant (optional):** If your build supports it, e.g. `SHOW WAREHOUSES LIKE '<name>'`.
107... 
108... **Stopping point — no warehouse with `USAGE` in the listing:** If **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** returns **no rows**, the primary role has **no** warehouse with **`USAGE`** in this result set—**do not** set **`query_warehouse`** from **`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** or invent a name. Tell the user they need **Workspace settings** or a **role / grant** change (e.g. **`USAGE` on WAREHOUSE`** from an admin), then re-run **sections 2 and 5** when they can run SQL again. For **new-app creation `write`s**, **remove** both **`query_warehouse`** and **`compute_pool`**, ensure **no** unresolved **`<...>`**, and tell the user **App Settings** (or Workspace) must supply warehouse and compute pool before **Run** succeeds—the **same** prompt / omit pattern as **section 2** and **section 4** (no pools in listing).
109... 
110... ---
111... 
112... ## 6. Warehouse and pool — validate against SHOW output
113... 
114... **Prerequisite:** **`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** must be set (**section 2**). If not, stop until the user updates **Workspace settings**—**unless** you are only writing **`snowflake.yml`** with **`query_warehouse`** and **`compute_pool`** **omitted** (**section 2**: **Exception — create without resolvable session resources**, **Omit both keys**, or empty-list stopping points in **sections 4–5**); then skip this section’s validation for that creation pass.
115... 
116... **Prerequisite:** **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** ran per **section 4** (optionally after **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`**, or without **`USE`** when **restricted** per **section 2**). **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** ran per **section 5** (after **`USE`** when allowed, or without **`USE`** when **restricted**). If secondary roles may have been re-enabled since the warehouse **`SHOW`** **and** the session allows **`USE`**, re-run **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`** and repeat **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** before interpreting warehouse results.
117... 
118... The active warehouse (**`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`**, **section 2**) must appear as a **`name`** in **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** (**section 5**), **unless** you are using the **omit-both-keys** path because that **`SHOW`** returned **no rows** (**section 5**). **Compute pool** names **only** from **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** (**section 4**); the chosen pool must appear there **unless** you are using the **omit-both-keys** path because **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** returned **no rows** (**section 4**).
119... 
120... ### Warehouse — `USAGE` from listing output (no separate `USE WAREHOUSE` step)
121... 
122... There is no need for a standalone **`USE WAREHOUSE`** preflight in this reference—the **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** result **is** the check. For pools, use **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** (**section 4**); there is no `USE COMPUTE POOL` in worksheets.
123... 
124... **Validate the session warehouse:** Confirm the value of **`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** appears as a warehouse **`name`** in **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** (or use a filtered variant if your build supports it, e.g. `SHOW WAREHOUSES LIKE '<name>'`). If it does **not** appear, the primary role lacks **`USAGE`** on that warehouse under the primary-role-only session—do not assume access. Ask the user to select a warehouse that **does** appear in that same result set (via **Workspace settings** / role change), then re-run **sections 2 and 5** and validate again.
125... 
126... ### Compute pool — already validated in section 4
127... 
128... **Section 4** is the validation: the chosen pool must appear in **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** (after **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`** when permitted, or without **`USE`** in a **restricted** session per **section 2**). If the listing was **empty**, you must **not** assert a pool name in **`snowflake.yml`**—use the **section 4** stopping point and **omit both keys** for new app creation. If Streamlit Run still fails with pool errors after a pool **was** chosen from that listing, treat it as a **product / grant** or App Settings mismatch: org admin may need to grant **`USAGE` on COMPUTE POOL** to the **developer role**, or the user must pick another pool from the same listing.
129... 
130... If Streamlit Run still fails with **warehouse** errors after **`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** appears in **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`**, treat it the same way: **product / grant**, App Settings mismatch, or wrong warehouse selected in the UI—do not invent warehouse names outside the **`SHOW`** listing.
131... 
132... ---
133... 
134... ## 7. Checklist before telling the user “you’re good to Run”
135... 
136... 1. **`CURRENT_ROLE()`** is the intended developer role for this app.
137... 2. **`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** is **non-null** *when you are validating session-backed YAML values*; if it was null and `snowflake.yml` still contains **`query_warehouse`** / **`compute_pool`** (or placeholders), the user was prompted to fix **Workspace settings** and you re-checked before proceeding. If **`snowflake.yml`** **omits** those keys (App Settings only), skip this check here and remind the user App Settings must provide warehouse and pool before **Run**.
138... 3. **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** ran (optionally after **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`** when permitted; if **`USE`** failed with a **restricted-session** error, **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** ran without **`USE`** per **section 2**).
139... 4. **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** ran: if the listing is **non-empty**, the account default pool from **`DEFAULT_STREAMLIT_COMPUTE_POOL`** appears there **or** you and the user chose a fallback **from that result set only** (or you rely on **App Settings** with both keys omitted). If the listing is **empty**, the user was prompted per **section 4** and, for new app creation, **`query_warehouse`** / **`compute_pool`** were **omitted** per **Omit both keys** in **section 2**.
140... 5. **`USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE`** ran successfully immediately before **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`**, **or** the session is **restricted** and you ran **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** without **`USE`** per **section 2** (again if the session allows **`USE`** and secondary roles may have changed since the pool `SHOW`, re-run **`USE`** then **`SHOW`**).
141... 6. **`CURRENT_WAREHOUSE()`** appears in **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** (warehouse **`USAGE`** listing; **compute pools** use item 4’s **`SHOW COMPUTE POOLS`** result), **or** **`SHOW WAREHOUSES`** returned **no rows** and the **section 5** stopping point / **omit both keys** path was followed.
142... 7. If any **`SHOW PARAMETERS IN ACCOUNT`** step failed, capture the error text for the user instead of inventing defaults.
143...

1... 
2... # Streamlit in Snowflake — runtime vs local
3... 
4... Use this guide when the app **runs inside Snowflake** (Streamlit in Snowflake on a warehouse, Snowflake Workspace / container runtime, or similar hosted SiS), or when you are writing code that must work both **locally** and **in Snowflake**. Vanilla `streamlit run` on a laptop assumes a normal filesystem, open PyPI/network access, and `.streamlit/secrets.toml` for credentials—those assumptions often **do not** hold in Snowflake. If you are unsure if an app is standalone or will run in Snowflake, ask the user.
5... 
6... For SQL/session patterns, see [snowflake-connection.md](snowflake-connection.md). For `snow` CLI, `snowflake.yml`, and local pre-deploy checks, see [snowflake-deployment.md](snowflake-deployment.md).
7... 
8... ---
9... 
10... ## Secrets and credentials
11... 
12... ### Inside Snowflake (hosted app)
13... 
14... - **Primary Snowflake access:** Use **`st.connection("snowflake")`** (and optionally **`type="snowflake-callers-rights"`** when viewers should execute with their own roles). The platform provides Snowflake session context; you usually **do not** commit or deploy `.streamlit/secrets.toml` **for the Snowflake connection** the way you do on a laptop.
15... - **Snowflake Workspace / container flows** may document a connection TTL (for example via environment variables). Follow the product or skill guidance for your environment when setting `ttl=` on `st.connection`.
16... - **Other secrets** (third-party API keys, tokens): Never hard-code. Use the secret or credential mechanisms your Snowflake account and Streamlit product surface support (for example app-level configuration where available). These are **not** interchangeable with “drop a `secrets.toml` in git.”
17... 
18... ### Local development of the same app
19... 
20... - Keep **`.streamlit/secrets.toml`** on your machine (and **`.gitignore`** it) so `st.connection("snowflake")` resolves `[connections.snowflake]` while you run `streamlit run` or tests. Derive `account` / `host` from `snow connection list` as in [snowflake-connection.md](snowflake-connection.md).
21... 
22... **Summary:** `st.secrets` / `secrets.toml` patterns in this repo mostly describe **local** wiring. In Snowflake, treat the Snowflake connection as **embedded**, and treat non-Snowflake secrets as **platform-managed**.
23... 
24... ---
25... 
26... ## External access, PyPI, and dependencies
27... 
28... - **Outbound calls** (PyPI, public HTTPS APIs, vendor LLM endpoints) require **external access integrations (EAIs)** and matching **network rules** in Snowflake. Names are **account-specific**; verify with `SHOW EXTERNAL ACCESS INTEGRATIONS` (or your admin) instead of hard-coding a global integration name.
29... - **Adding packages** (including third-party Streamlit components from PyPI) follows the same rules as any dependency: the runtime must be allowed to reach the index or wheel source. Some Workspace setups use a **fixed pre-installed** dependency set unless `pyproject.toml` is changed **and** PyPI access is configured—changing dependencies without EAI can fail at runtime.
30... - Do not assume `uv pip install` or unrestricted internet from inside the hosted app; align with [snowflake-deployment.md](snowflake-deployment.md) and your org’s networking policy.
31... 
32... **Docs:** [Streamlit in Snowflake — dependency management](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/streamlit/app-development/dependency-management), [External network access overview](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/external-network-access/external-network-access-overview).
33... 
34... ---
35... 
36... ## Files, artifacts, and uploads
37... 
38... ### Only deployed files exist at runtime
39... 
40... - Any path you open (`open(...)`, `pd.read_csv("data.csv")`, `torch.load("model.pt")`, images, fonts, CCv2 assets, etc.) must refer to files that are actually **shipped with the app**. In Snowflake, that means listing them under **`artifacts`** in `snowflake.yml` (or the equivalent for your deployment path). Laptop-only paths will raise **file not found** in production.
41... 
42... ### Durable data belongs in Snowflake
43... 
44... - Prefer **tables, stages, and Snowflake APIs** for durable or large data instead of writing to arbitrary host paths for persistence.
45... 
46... ### Upload widgets (`st.file_uploader`, chat file attachments)
47... 
48... - Uploads are handled **in the app process** for the session. Very large files can hit **memory or request limits** in hosted runtimes. Prefer size limits, chunking, or uploading to a **Snowflake stage** / table for large binaries.
49... 
50... ### Static assets and `enableStaticServing`
51... 
52... - Theme and static file guidance still applies: files must be **in the deployed bundle** to be served. Local-only static directories are not visible after deploy unless included in artifacts.
53... 
54... ---
55... 
56... ## Quick checklist (Snowflake-hosted)
57... 
58... 1. Snowflake connection via **`st.connection("snowflake")`** — no laptop-only `secrets.toml` requirement for embedded identity.
59... 2. **Artifacts** list every runtime file (Python, config, data, static assets).
60... 3. **Outbound network / PyPI** — EAIs and app settings match what `pyproject.toml` and APIs need.
61... 4. **Secrets** — no credentials in source; use supported Snowflake / app secret patterns for non-Snowflake keys.

2... # Streamlit dashboards
3... 
4... Compose metrics, charts, and data into clean dashboard layouts.
5... 
6... ## Cards with borders
7... 
8... Use `border=True` to create visual cards. Supported on `st.container`, `st.metric`, `st.columns`, and `st.form`:
9... 
10... ```python
11... # Container card
12... with st.container(border=True):
13...     st.subheader("Sales Overview")
14...     st.line_chart(sales_data)
15... 
16... # Metric card
17... st.metric("Revenue", "$1.2M", "+12%", border=True)
18... 
19... # Column cards
20... for col in st.columns(3, border=True):
21...     with col:
22...         st.metric("Users", "1.2k")
23... ```
24... 
25... ## Card labels
26... 
27... Add context to cards with headers or bold text:
28... 
29... ```python
30... # With subheader
31... with st.container(border=True):
32...     st.subheader("Monthly Trends")
33...     st.line_chart(data)
34... 
35... # With bold label
36... with st.container(border=True):
37...     st.markdown("**Top Products**")
38...     st.dataframe(top_products)
39... ```
40... 
41... ## KPI rows
42... 
43... Use horizontal containers for responsive metric rows:
44... 
45... ```python
46... with st.container(horizontal=True):
47...     st.metric("Revenue", "$1.2M", "-7%", border=True)
48...     st.metric("Users", "762k", "+12%", border=True)
49...     st.metric("Orders", "1.4k", "+5%", border=True)
50... ```
51... 
52... Horizontal containers wrap on smaller screens. Prefer them over `st.columns` for metric rows.
53... 
54... ## Metrics with sparklines
55... 
56... Add trend context with `chart_data`:
57... 
58... ```python
59... weekly_values = [700, 720, 715, 740, 762, 755, 780]
60... 
61... st.metric(
62...     "Active Users",
63...     "780k",
64...     "+3.2%",
65...     border=True,
66...     chart_data=weekly_values,
67...     chart_type="line",  # or "bar"
68... )
69... ```
70... 
71... Sparklines show y-values only—use for evenly-spaced data like daily/weekly snapshots.
72... 
73... ## Dashboard layout
74... 
75... Combine cards into a dashboard:
76... 
77... ```python
78... # KPI row
79... with st.container(horizontal=True):
80...     st.metric("Revenue", "$1.2M", "-7%", border=True, chart_data=rev_trend, chart_type="line")
81...     st.metric("Users", "762k", "+12%", border=True, chart_data=user_trend, chart_type="line")
82...     st.metric("Orders", "1.4k", "+5%", border=True, chart_data=order_trend, chart_type="bar")
83... 
84... # Charts row
85... col1, col2 = st.columns(2)
86... with col1:
87...     with st.container(border=True):
88...         st.subheader("Revenue by Region")
89...         st.bar_chart(region_data, x="region", y="revenue")
90... 
91... with col2:
92...     with st.container(border=True):
93...         st.subheader("Monthly Trend")
94...         st.line_chart(monthly_data, x="month", y="value")
95... 
96... # Data table
97... with st.container(border=True):
98...     st.subheader("Recent Orders")
99...     st.dataframe(orders_df, hide_index=True)
100... ```

103... 
104... Put filters in the sidebar to maximize dashboard space:

import os
import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(page_title="E.D.I.E. — Insurance Control Center", page_icon="🏢", layout="wide")

conn = st.connection("snowflake", ttl=os.getenv("SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTION_TTL"))


@st.cache_data(ttl=300)
def run_query(sql):
    return conn.query(sql)


st.title("E.D.I.E. — Insurance Control Center")
st.caption("Enterprise Data & Intelligence Engine | Insurance AI Hub")

tab1, tab2, tab3, tab4, tab5, tab6 = st.tabs([
    "Customer 360", "Policy Analytics", "Claims Intelligence",
    "Billing & Revenue", "Risk & Retention", "Data Quality"
])

# --- TAB 1: Customer 360 ---
with tab1:
    st.header("Customer 360")

    c1, c2, c3, c4 = st.columns(4)
    totals = run_query("SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, COUNT(DISTINCT STATE) AS states FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.CUSTOMERS")
    c1.metric("Total Customers", f"{totals['TOTAL'].iloc[0]:,}")
    c2.metric("States Covered", totals['STATES'].iloc[0])

    nulls = run_query("SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN EMAIL IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS null_emails, SUM(CASE WHEN PHONE IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS null_phones FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.CUSTOMERS")
    c3.metric("Missing Emails", int(nulls['NULL_EMAILS'].iloc[0]))
    c4.metric("Missing Phones", int(nulls['NULL_PHONES'].iloc[0]))

    col1, col2 = st.columns(2)
    with col1:
        with st.container(border=True):
            st.subheader("Risk Tier Distribution")
            risk = run_query("SELECT RISK_TIER, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.CUSTOMERS GROUP BY RISK_TIER ORDER BY CNT DESC")
            st.bar_chart(risk, x="RISK_TIER", y="CNT")

    with col2:
        with st.container(border=True):
            st.subheader("Customer Segment")
            seg = run_query("SELECT SEGMENT, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.CUSTOMERS GROUP BY SEGMENT ORDER BY CNT DESC")
            st.bar_chart(seg, x="SEGMENT", y="CNT")

    with st.container(border=True):
        st.subheader("Credit Score by Risk Tier")
        credit = run_query("SELECT RISK_TIER, ROUND(AVG(CREDIT_SCORE)) AS AVG_CREDIT, MIN(CREDIT_SCORE) AS MIN_CREDIT, MAX(CREDIT_SCORE) AS MAX_CREDIT FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.CUSTOMERS GROUP BY RISK_TIER ORDER BY AVG_CREDIT DESC")
        st.dataframe(credit, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)

# --- TAB 2: Policy Analytics ---
with tab2:
    st.header("Policy Analytics")

    pol_totals = run_query("SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_policies, ROUND(SUM(PREMIUM_AMOUNT), 2) AS total_premium, ROUND(AVG(COVERAGE_AMOUNT), 0) AS avg_coverage FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.POLICIES")
    c1, c2, c3 = st.columns(3)
    c1.metric("Total Policies", f"{pol_totals['TOTAL_POLICIES'].iloc[0]:,}")
    c2.metric("Total Premium", f"${pol_totals['TOTAL_PREMIUM'].iloc[0]:,.0f}")
    c3.metric("Avg Coverage", f"${pol_totals['AVG_COVERAGE'].iloc[0]:,.0f}")

    col1, col2 = st.columns(2)
    with col1:
        with st.container(border=True):
            st.subheader("Policies by Type")
            by_type = run_query("SELECT POLICY_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS CNT, ROUND(AVG(PREMIUM_AMOUNT), 2) AS AVG_PREMIUM FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.POLICIES GROUP BY POLICY_TYPE ORDER BY CNT DESC")
            st.bar_chart(by_type, x="POLICY_TYPE", y="CNT")

    with col2:
        with st.container(border=True):
            st.subheader("Plan Tier Distribution")
            by_tier = run_query("SELECT PLAN_TIER, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.POLICIES GROUP BY PLAN_TIER ORDER BY CNT DESC")
            st.bar_chart(by_tier, x="PLAN_TIER", y="CNT")

    with st.container(border=True):
        st.subheader("Policy Status & Renewal")
        status = run_query("SELECT STATUS, RENEWAL_STATUS, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.POLICIES GROUP BY STATUS, RENEWAL_STATUS ORDER BY CNT DESC")
        st.dataframe(status, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)

# --- TAB 3: Claims Intelligence ---
with tab3:
    st.header("Claims Intelligence")

    cl_totals = run_query("SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_claims, ROUND(SUM(CLAIM_AMOUNT), 2) AS total_claimed, ROUND(AVG(FRAUD_SCORE), 2) AS avg_fraud, ROUND(AVG(RESOLUTION_DAYS), 1) AS avg_resolution FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.CLAIMS")
    c1, c2, c3, c4 = st.columns(4)
    c1.metric("Total Claims", f"{cl_totals['TOTAL_CLAIMS'].iloc[0]:,}")
    c2.metric("Total Claimed", f"${cl_totals['TOTAL_CLAIMED'].iloc[0]:,.0f}")
    c3.metric("Avg Fraud Score", cl_totals['AVG_FRAUD'].iloc[0])
    c4.metric("Avg Resolution (days)", cl_totals['AVG_RESOLUTION'].iloc[0])

    col1, col2 = st.columns(2)
    with col1:
        with st.container(border=True):
            st.subheader("Monthly Claims Trend")
            monthly = run_query("SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', CLAIM_DATE)::DATE AS MONTH, COUNT(*) AS CLAIMS FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.CLAIMS GROUP BY MONTH ORDER BY MONTH")
            st.line_chart(monthly, x="MONTH", y="CLAIMS")

    with col2:
        with st.container(border=True):
            st.subheader("Fraud Score Distribution")
            fraud = run_query("""
                SELECT
                    CASE
                        WHEN FRAUD_SCORE < 20 THEN '0-20 Low'
                        WHEN FRAUD_SCORE < 40 THEN '20-40 Normal'
                        WHEN FRAUD_SCORE < 60 THEN '40-60 Elevated'
                        WHEN FRAUD_SCORE < 80 THEN '60-80 High'
                        ELSE '80-100 Critical'
                    END AS FRAUD_BAND, COUNT(*) AS CNT
                FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.CLAIMS GROUP BY FRAUD_BAND ORDER BY FRAUD_BAND
            """)
            st.bar_chart(fraud, x="FRAUD_BAND", y="CNT")

    with st.container(border=True):
        st.subheader("High Fraud Claims (Score > 80)")
        high_fraud = run_query("SELECT CLAIM_ID, POLICY_ID, CLAIM_TYPE, CLAIM_AMOUNT, FRAUD_SCORE, STATUS, CAUSE_OF_LOSS FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.CLAIMS WHERE FRAUD_SCORE > 80 ORDER BY FRAUD_SCORE DESC LIMIT 20")
        st.dataframe(high_fraud, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)

# --- TAB 4: Billing & Revenue ---
with tab4:
    st.header("Billing & Revenue")

    bill_totals = run_query("SELECT COUNT(*) AS invoices, ROUND(SUM(OUTSTANDING_BALANCE), 2) AS total_outstanding, ROUND(SUM(LATE_FEE), 2) AS total_late_fees, SUM(CASE WHEN PAYMENT_STATUS = 'Overdue' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS overdue_count FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.BILLING")
    c1, c2, c3, c4 = st.columns(4)
    c1.metric("Total Invoices", f"{bill_totals['INVOICES'].iloc[0]:,}")
    c2.metric("Outstanding Balance", f"${bill_totals['TOTAL_OUTSTANDING'].iloc[0]:,.0f}")
    c3.metric("Late Fees Collected", f"${bill_totals['TOTAL_LATE_FEES'].iloc[0]:,.0f}")
    c4.metric("Overdue Invoices", f"{bill_totals['OVERDUE_COUNT'].iloc[0]:,}")

    col1, col2 = st.columns(2)
    with col1:
        with st.container(border=True):
            st.subheader("Payment Status")
            pay_status = run_query("SELECT PAYMENT_STATUS, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.BILLING GROUP BY PAYMENT_STATUS ORDER BY CNT DESC")
            st.bar_chart(pay_status, x="PAYMENT_STATUS", y="CNT")

    with col2:
        with st.container(border=True):
            st.subheader("Payment Methods")
            pay_method = run_query("SELECT PAYMENT_METHOD, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.BILLING WHERE PAYMENT_METHOD IS NOT NULL GROUP BY PAYMENT_METHOD ORDER BY CNT DESC")
            st.bar_chart(pay_method, x="PAYMENT_METHOD", y="CNT")

# --- TAB 5: Risk & Retention ---
with tab5:
    st.header("Risk & Retention")

    risk_totals = run_query("SELECT COUNT(*) AS at_risk_count, ROUND(SUM(REVENUE_AT_RISK), 2) AS total_revenue_at_risk, ROUND(AVG(CHURN_PROBABILITY), 4) AS avg_churn FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.AT_RISK_POLICIES")
    c1, c2, c3 = st.columns(3)
    c1.metric("Policies At Risk", f"{risk_totals['AT_RISK_COUNT'].iloc[0]:,}")
    c2.metric("Revenue At Risk", f"${risk_totals['TOTAL_REVENUE_AT_RISK'].iloc[0]:,.0f}")
    c3.metric("Avg Churn Probability", f"{risk_totals['AVG_CHURN'].iloc[0]:.2%}")

    col1, col2 = st.columns(2)
    with col1:
        with st.container(border=True):
            st.subheader("Risk Category")
            risk_cat = run_query("SELECT RISK_CATEGORY, COUNT(*) AS CNT, ROUND(SUM(REVENUE_AT_RISK), 2) AS REVENUE FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.AT_RISK_POLICIES GROUP BY RISK_CATEGORY ORDER BY REVENUE DESC")
            st.dataframe(risk_cat, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)

    with col2:
        with st.container(border=True):
            st.subheader("Retention Actions")
            actions = run_query("SELECT RETENTION_ACTION, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.AT_RISK_POLICIES GROUP BY RETENTION_ACTION ORDER BY CNT DESC")
            st.bar_chart(actions, x="RETENTION_ACTION", y="CNT")

    with st.container(border=True):
        st.subheader("Top 15 Highest Risk Policies")
        top_risk = run_query("SELECT RISK_ID, POLICY_ID, CUSTOMER_ID, RISK_CATEGORY, CHURN_PROBABILITY, REVENUE_AT_RISK, MISSED_PAYMENTS_COUNT, NPS_SCORE FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.ANALYTICS.AT_RISK_POLICIES ORDER BY CHURN_PROBABILITY DESC LIMIT 15")
        st.dataframe(top_risk, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)

# --- TAB 6: Data Quality ---
with tab6:
    st.header("Data Quality Observability")

    dq_totals = run_query("SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_rules, SUM(CASE WHEN IS_ACTIVE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_rules FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.DATA_QUALITY.DQ_RULES")
    fail_count = run_query("SELECT COUNT(*) AS fails FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.DATA_QUALITY.DQ_RESULTS WHERE STATUS = 'Fail'")
    c1, c2, c3 = st.columns(3)
    c1.metric("DQ Rules", int(dq_totals['TOTAL_RULES'].iloc[0]))
    c2.metric("Active Rules", int(dq_totals['ACTIVE_RULES'].iloc[0]))
    c3.metric("Total Failures (90d)", int(fail_count['FAILS'].iloc[0]))

    col1, col2 = st.columns(2)
    with col1:
        with st.container(border=True):
            st.subheader("Latest Table Scores")
            scores = run_query("""
                SELECT TABLE_NAME, OVERALL_SCORE, COMPLETENESS_SCORE, VALIDITY_SCORE, TIMELINESS_SCORE, TREND
                FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.DATA_QUALITY.DQ_SCORES
                QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY TABLE_NAME ORDER BY SCORE_DATE DESC) = 1
                ORDER BY OVERALL_SCORE
            """)
            st.dataframe(scores, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)

    with col2:
        with st.container(border=True):
            st.subheader("Most Failing Rules")
            failing = run_query("""
                SELECT r.RULE_NAME, r.TARGET_TABLE, r.SEVERITY, COUNT(*) AS FAIL_COUNT
                FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.DATA_QUALITY.DQ_RESULTS res
                JOIN INSURANCE_AI_HUB.DATA_QUALITY.DQ_RULES r ON res.RULE_ID = r.RULE_ID
                WHERE res.STATUS = 'Fail'
                GROUP BY r.RULE_NAME, r.TARGET_TABLE, r.SEVERITY
                ORDER BY FAIL_COUNT DESC LIMIT 10
            """)
            st.dataframe(failing, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)

    with st.container(border=True):
        st.subheader("Unhealthiest Columns")
        col_health = run_query("""
            SELECT TABLE_NAME, COLUMN_NAME, ROUND(AVG(HEALTH_SCORE), 2) AS AVG_HEALTH,
                   ROUND(AVG(NULL_RATE), 2) AS AVG_NULL_RATE, ROUND(AVG(OUTLIER_RATE), 2) AS AVG_OUTLIER_RATE
            FROM INSURANCE_AI_HUB.DATA_QUALITY.DQ_COLUMN_HEALTH
            GROUP BY TABLE_NAME, COLUMN_NAME
            ORDER BY AVG_HEALTH LIMIT 10
        """)
        st.dataframe(col_health, hide_index=True, use_container_width=True)

# Footer
st.divider()
